title: Farfus wins from pole in Valencia as Paffett's title lead shrinks to three points
dek: Augusto Farfus won from pole by 8.406 seconds for BMW Team RBM in Valencia, while Gary Paffett's retirement let Bruno Spengler, sixth after a drive-through, cut the title gap to three points.

chapters.title: Three drivers left in the title fight
text: The ninth of the ten races of the 2012 DTM season, at the Circuit Ricardo Tormo on Sunday 30 September, began with the championship down to three names. Gary Paffett had led the table since the opening race and arrived with 127 points, 11 clear of Bruno Spengler on 116, with Jamie Green third on 108. Mike Rockenfeller, fourth on 75, could not reach Paffett's total even by winning both remaining races, so the title was a matter of the two HWA Mercedes drivers and the Schnitzer BMW.

Spengler was the man in form. Two weeks earlier he had won at Oschersleben, 0.629 seconds ahead of Paffett, adding to his earlier wins at the Lausitzring and the Nürburgring, and in the races since the Red Bull Ring he had cut a 40-point deficit to 11.

Valencia itself came with a new variable. The surface had been relaid since the teams' tests, and both Spengler and Joey Hand talked of grip that differed from what they had found earlier in the year. BMW's rookie Augusto Farfus, at the wheel of the Team RBM car, said the balance had felt right from his first laps on Friday.

chapters.title: Farfus beats the Audis to pole
text: Saturday's qualifying went to Farfus. The BMW Team RBM driver set 1:26.446 in the final session, 0.310 seconds quicker than Edoardo Mortara's Rosberg Audi on 1:26.756. Filipe Albuquerque, in the second Rosberg car, took third on 1:26.894 and Adrien Tambay fourth for Abt, so the first two rows read Audi, Audi, Audi around a lone BMW.

Mike Rockenfeller was fifth for Phoenix, Andy Priaulx sixth in the second RBM BMW, then came Timo Scheider and Mattias Ekström in the Abt Sportsline Audis, Dirk Werner ninth for Schnitzer and Miguel Molina tenth in the other Phoenix Audi. Farfus said the car's balance suited his driving style as well as anywhere he had been this season.

The title contenders fared badly. Spengler could manage only 12th and Martin Tomczyk 11th, both of them falling out of the second part by a matter of thousandths. For Mercedes it was worse: Robert Wickens, 14th, was the quickest of their eight cars, Paffett was 16th, Green 18th and Ralf Schumacher last of the 22 starters. Paffett said the fresh tyres had not given him enough grip, but that he expected much better race pace. He would start four places behind Spengler.

chapters.title: Chaos in the first corners
text: Farfus led away from pole, but behind him the opening corners were a tangle. Tomczyk's BMW was damaged in the melee, and Roberto Merhi's Mercedes was wrecked in the same incident, so that Tomczyk never completed a lap and Merhi lasted one. Within a corner or two Paffett, up from 16th, tried to get inside Hand's BMW and the two touched. Hand continued, but Paffett's Mercedes was damaged, and he would later serve a time penalty in the pits for the contact. Robert Wickens was out within three laps as well.

Spengler had gained places from 12th and was up to ninth when the stewards gave him a drive-through penalty for a jump start. He insisted over the radio that he had not moved early, but his team ordered him in and he served it on lap six. After the stop he rejoined still ahead of Paffett and began to climb again.

chapters.title: Attrition costs Audi and Mercedes
text: At the front Farfus had built a cushion of about five seconds over Mortara by the time of the first stops and was never under real pressure; a slipping wheel gun at his second stop was the only moment of alarm. Heat was a factor: Marquardt said race day was hotter than the rest of the weekend and the tyres wore quickly.

Behind him the race kept thinning out. Green, who had spent the early laps well down the order after his poor qualifying, was given a drive-through for leaving the track. Molina's Audi struck the wall at mid-distance after a technical failure, and Paffett parked his damaged Mercedes after 27 laps, scoring nothing. Scheider, who had been running on the podium course, stopped on lap 29 with drivetrain trouble.

chapters.title: Farfus wins, Spengler fights back to sixth
text: With around seven laps to go a mechanical problem dropped Mortara out of second place. He was classified 16th, eight laps down, and that left two Abt Audis on the podium: Tambay was second, 8.406 seconds behind Farfus, with Ekström a further 0.561 seconds back in third. Albuquerque was fourth and Rockenfeller fifth, 28.066 seconds behind the winner, so Audi took five of the first seven places.

Spengler finished sixth, 39.831 seconds behind Farfus, after passing Priaulx and Rahel Frey in the closing stages and setting the fastest lap of the race, a 1:27.116 on lap 32. The move drew a row. Priaulx and Frey were in close contact on lap 40 as Spengler closed on them, Audi's Wolfgang Ullrich said the BMW drivers had reached into the "bottom drawer", and Priaulx then let Frey through. She took seventh, with Priaulx eighth, Werner ninth and Green tenth for the last point. The BMW total of four cars in the top ten was Farfus, Spengler, Priaulx and Werner.

chapters.title: Three points between Paffett and Spengler
text: Farfus had taken his first DTM victory, and the first by a Brazilian driver in the series. He said he cried through the last half-lap and called it a privilege to win in his rookie season. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt said he had dominated from pole and fully deserved the win.

The title picture changed completely. Paffett's zero left him on 127, while Spengler's sixth place was worth eight points and took him to 124, three behind with one race to go. Green, 10th, had 109 and was still 18 off the lead, and Rockenfeller on 85 and Ekström on 81 had slipped out of reach. Over the last five races Paffett had given away 37 points to Spengler. Paffett wrote that it had been a nightmare weekend, and said he was looking forward to Hockenheim.

Audi had the strongest day of the three manufacturers. Tambay and Ekström shared the podium, Albuquerque and Rockenfeller followed and Frey took seventh, while Mortara and Scheider were left to rue mechanical trouble from strong positions. Three title contenders were handed penalties on the same afternoon: a drive-through for Spengler, a time penalty at the stop for Paffett and a drive-through for Green, and all three lost time. It was a bleak day for Mercedes: their best finisher was Green in tenth, David Coulthard was 11th, Christian Vietoris 12th, and Susie Wolff and Ralf Schumacher were a lap down in 13th and 14th. For BMW, Hand and Tomczyk had a poor afternoon. Hand was hit early, finished 15th and four laps down, and Tomczyk's race ended at the start. Marquardt said both Team RMG drivers were unlucky.

The season would be decided at Hockenheim on 21 October, three weeks later. Three points separated Paffett and Spengler, and the maximum for a win was 25, so either could take the title, and Green could still do it as well if he won and both rivals finished well down.

facts.v: Augusto Farfus won from pole in 1:08:22.522 over 46 laps, 8.406 seconds ahead of Adrien Tambay, for his first DTM victory and the first by a Brazilian driver.

facts.v: Bruno Spengler finished sixth after a drive-through penalty, while Gary Paffett retired without scoring, so the gap at the top fell from 11 points to three (127 to 124).

one.label: Motorsport-Total: Viel Action in Valencia - Farfus siegt, Spengler holt auf

facts.v: Martin Tomczyk and Roberto Merhi were out within the first lap, Paffett touched Joey Hand on the opening lap and later served a time penalty, and Robert Wickens was out by lap three.
BMW said Sunday was the hottest day of the weekend and its cars had to contend with quickly wearing tyres, yet four BMWs finished in the top ten.

facts.t: Mercedes at the back of the grid
facts.v: All eight Mercedes started 14th or lower, led by Robert Wickens in 14th, and the best of them at the finish was Jamie Green in tenth.
